title: Which layer restores the fence placement
subtitle: A decision ticket for the map "Map: a development workshop that drives the product".
question: Which layer restores the fence placement when the control service kills a lifecycle verb at its timeout: the fence command, the control service, or a longer timeout for a verb that rebuilds a snapshot?
baseline_note: these steps are the same in every option
legend: The steps before the limit are the same in every option. The shaded band in each diagram holds the steps that the option changes, and the band carries a note that names the change.
situation: The service runs `uv run monitor-agent-egress-fence <verb>` with a limit of 900 seconds. The fence command releases the placement before it rebuilds the workshops and applies the fence after them.
At the limit the service sends SIGKILL to `uv` and closes the pipe to the fence command.
The fence command is a child of `uv`, so it survives the kill. It writes its report only after its apply phase, so it reaches that phase.
The `workshop` command dies of SIGPIPE when it writes to the closed pipe. `workshopd` keeps the rebuild running.
The apply phase then runs while the workshop is still rebuilding. The agent instance is absent, so the apply faults and the placement stays released.
Nothing retries the apply. The service discards the output of a verb that times out, so the audit line `refresh 2` does not show what the fence command did.

actors.name: Control service
actors.role: runs the verb and holds the limit.

actors.name: uv
actors.role: starts the fence command as its own child.

actors.name: Fence command
actors.role: releases the placement, runs the workshop command, then applies the fence.

actors.name: Workshop client
actors.role: drives workshopd, which rebuilds the instance and runs the SDK install.

actors.name: Fence placement
actors.role: is the fence bridge and the fixed address on the instance NIC.

options.name: Option A
options.headline: The control service applies the fence after it kills a verb
options.changes: The service runs the apply as a separate command after it kills a verb, and retries it while the workshop rebuilds.
options.leaves_open: A run where the fence command itself is killed outside the service.
options.what: The service runs the fence command's apply as a separate command with its own timeout after a verb times out, and retries that apply while the workshop is still rebuilding.
options.window: The window ends when that apply finishes, which is after the rebuild ends and not before.
why: The service is the layer that kills the verb, so it is the only layer that knows the placement was left released.
The service needs no new knowledge of the fence. It already runs the apply verb through the same runner.
The service can write the restore to the audit log, which it cannot do today for a verb that times out.

prefix: C->>D: rebuild the instance and install the SDK
Note over D: the install takes about 24 minutes
Note over S: the limit of 900 seconds passes
U--xF: the pipe to the fence command closes
C--xD: the workshop client dies of SIGPIPE
F->>P: the apply phase runs while the agent instance is absent
steps: Note over S: the service retries the apply while the workshop rebuilds

options.name: Option B
options.headline: The fence command applies the fence after the kill
options.changes: The fence command waits for the rebuild and places the placement itself.
options.leaves_open: A run where the fence command itself is killed.
options.what: The fence command waits for the rebuild to finish and places the placement itself, the way it places the placement after a lifecycle command that fails.
options.window: The window ends when the apply of the fence command finishes.
why: The fence command survives the kill of its parent, so it reaches its apply phase. It writes its report only after that phase.
The fence command cannot tell that the service killed its parent, and it cannot tell a rebuild that is still running from a rebuild that failed, so its wait has no end that it can name.

options.name: Option C
options.headline: A longer timeout for a verb that rebuilds a snapshot
options.restores: The fence command, as it is today
options.changes: The value of the limit for a verb that rebuilds a snapshot, so no kill happens.
options.leaves_open: A run that exceeds the new limit, which has the same hole.
options.what: The install of the hermes SDK took about 24 minutes and the limit is 900 seconds, so a longer limit lets the refresh finish inside the limit.
options.window: The ordinary case stays out of the kill, so the fence command's own apply phase places the placement after the rebuild.
why: The 3600 seconds of the conformance suite belong to that suite and do not bound the service on the host.
The change is to the value of the limit and not to the recovery.

options.name: Option D
options.headline: The service applies the fence, and the timeout for a rebuilding verb grows
options.changes: The value of the limit, and the apply the service runs after it kills a verb.
options.leaves_open: A run where the fence command itself is killed outside the service.
options.what: The service applies the fence after it kills a verb, and a verb that rebuilds a snapshot gets a longer limit, so the ordinary case never reaches a kill.
options.window: The window ends when the apply of the service finishes, in the case where a verb reached the limit.
why: The service covers the kill, and the longer limit keeps the common case out of the hole.
Two changes in two layers, and the value of the new limit is a separate decision.

answer.summary: The control service restores the fence placement. It runs the fence command's apply as a separate command after a verb times out, and retries that apply while the workshop is still rebuilding. The fence command changes nothing.
answer.detail: The value of the timeout for a verb that rebuilds a snapshot is a separate decision, and it is compatible with this answer.

not_verified: What the fence command did after the timeout on 2026-11-15. The record of that run does not hold it.
The step where the apply phase ran while the agent instance was absent is the reading that fits the record, not a measurement.
